A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Implicit Bias VI work. Their main text, figures, equations, and complete supplementary Sections S1–S3 support reliable comparison across pagination and section-number changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original image-classification, corruption-robustness, hyperparameter-transfer, and optimization experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and reports additional SWAG comparisons on the classification and corruption benchmarks.

M1.justification: The expected-loss objective, Gaussian covariance-factor parametrization, variational maximal-update scaling, and training and prediction procedures are retained. Rewritten explanations and revised theoretical arguments do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, their corruption benchmarks, and the same synthetic demonstrations. Table S1 and the supplementary experiments show unchanged dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: SWAG is added to the comparisons in Figures 4, 5, and S10–S12. Standard networks, temperature scaling, both last-layer Laplace variants, mean-field weight-space VI, and deep ensembles remain.

E3.justification: The added SWAG evaluation introduces averaging beginning halfway through training, with updates every epoch (Section S3.3.1). Previously stated splits, architectures, learning rates, training budgets, metrics, and prediction sample counts are unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing corruption-robustness analyses gain SWAG comparisons under standard and maximal-update parametrizations (Figures 5 and S12). The NLL-overfitting case study and sensitivity analyses involving width, parameter samples, learning rate, and momentum are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Benchmark figures replace individual seed dots with vertical error bars, changing uncertainty reporting without defining the bars' statistical meaning. Five-seed averaging and the stated 95% confidence intervals in Figures S3–S6 remain unchanged; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: SWAG results are added throughout the benchmark comparisons, and numerous IBVI, weight-space VI, and TinyImageNet ensemble entries change. IBVI's CIFAR-10-C error changes approximately from 0.275 to 0.260 in Figure 5, but from 0.248 to 0.264 under maximal-update parametrization in Figure S12, reversing its ranking against the ensemble there. Newly reported SWAG results lead top-5 accuracy on the two larger corruption benchmarks under maximal-update parametrization.

T1.justification: New Theorems S3–S4 prove finite-time predictive-error/variance identities for noiseless, prior-generated linear data, plus covariance-trace monotonicity under a learning-rate condition. The classification proof replaces its time-dependent residual offset and finite-variation argument with a fixed offset and covariance-factor bounds. The main-text sample/batch/momentum scaling conjecture is removed. The rewritten proof also introduces a matrix-order error in Equation S66.

C1.justification: The central claims about implicit regularization, linear-model characterization, hyperparameter transfer, and competitive performance at low overhead remain. v2 adds the standalone open-source inferno implementation as an explicit contribution; its stronger emphasis on robustness largely restates existing scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies extrapolation of the linear Wasserstein characterization to deep networks, whose implicit bias may be more complex. It replaces the specific assertion about Cholesky factorization with an open-problem statement about arbitrary covariance parametrizations, and uses the already-existing ensemble-equivalence result to interpret empirical similarities.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports the inferno implementation and supplies its repository link. It also documents SWAG's implementation sources and averaging settings. Existing IBVI implementation, hardware, architecture, and training details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the SWAG reference by Maddox et al. and two works supporting the discussion of support vectors in overparameterized classification. Bayesian-deep-learning background and stochastic-weight-averaging positioning are expanded; most other citation changes are reordering or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, background, and method motivation are substantially rewritten around robust model averaging and selection among zero-training-error distributions. Large portions of the classification proof are also reorganized and re-explained, extending beyond local copyediting.

P2.justification: The probabilistic loss landscape in Figure S1 is redrawn. Benchmark plots add SWAG legends and error bars, adjust axes, and relocate Figure 4 beside Figure 5. Existing plot grids and Table S1 are retained. Figure S8 acquires a broken equation reference.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1's asymptotic analysis, v2 adds useful finite-time uncertainty guarantees under explicit, restrictive linear-model assumptions. SWAG comparisons, clearer applicability qualifications, and implementation access information also strengthen the paper. These gains are tempered by undefined error bars, the matrix-order error in Equation S66, and the broken Figure S8 reference, supporting a limited net improvement.
